title: Retry check-skipping for prose-only changes without breaking the gate
summary: Re-do the earlier job (retry of 045315-qaph) that lets a job's checks be skipped when the change touches only a named set of paths (for example docs or studies JSON). The last attempt failed because athena.toml gained `skip_when_only` in the same commit as the parser change, and the gate parsed it with the old parser. This reading lands the parser, runner, tests and docs, and leaves athena.toml untouched.

defaults_applied.how: New unit tests for config parsing, path matching, and the skip decision. cargo test and clippy must stay clean.
The skip rule is enforced in code and gets a row in docs/enforcement.md.
Parser, runner, and docs only. athena.toml stays untouched to avoid the bootstrap failure.
Recovered the intent from the referenced job's failure text and the repository.
Docs and comments explain the path-matching rules for an outside reader.

assumptions: The failure was a bootstrap problem: the gate judges a commit with the parent's parser, so a new athena.toml key cannot land in the same commit as the parser that reads it.

I cannot see the original request (045315-qaph). I infer it from the failure and the verifier notes: skip checks for docs-only or studies-JSON-only changes, with tests named a_studies_json_only_change_runs_every_check and a docs-only test, and a row M31 in docs/enforcement.md.
The feature is inert until a follow-up edits athena.toml. This is the smallest change that passes the gate.

acceptance_criteria.text: CheckConfig in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs accepts an optional `skip_when_only` list. An absent list means the check always runs. Existing configurations parse unchanged.

athena.toml is NOT modified. It must contain no `skip_when_only` key, so the gate's old parser accepts the landing commit. A note (docs or CHANGELOG) says enabling the key is a separate follow-up job after this one lands.

The check runner skips a check only when every changed path matches a named set in the configuration. An empty change list or any non-matching path runs the check. The skip is recorded in the run output with a note, not silently.
The path-matching rules (including the `*.ext` suffix form matching at any depth) are documented in code comments or docs/enforcement.md.
docs/enforcement.md has a row for the new mechanism that names its tests.

Run `cargo test --locked`. All tests pass, including new unit tests for config parsing, path matching, and skip versus run decisions. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`. Both are clean.

out_of_scope: Adding `skip_when_only` or any new key to athena.toml (follow-up job)
Changing the gate's parser or the history check
Changing records/ or the owner's files
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference, because this is a multi-crate change and a retry. Acceptance is lower than the reference because I could not see the original request and am inferring the feature.
